page: Amazon Web Services r5ad.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 7571 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 8 dedicated vCPUs spanning 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core operating at a base frequency of 2.2 GHz. The compute profile includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 8 MB of L3 cache, backed by instruction support for AVX, AES-NI, and SHA-NI cryptographic operations.

Memory capacity is configured at 64.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. A key distinction of the r5ad family is the integration of 300 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system contains no physical GPUs, focusing its compute and IO entirely on system memory and low-latency ephemeral disk operations.

Benchmark results demonstrate modest per-thread and vector performance typical of older AMD Zen-based silicon. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 727.0 and a multi-core score of 2943.0, both placing in the lower percentiles. In stress-ng evaluations, single-core and multi-core CPU metrics measured at 591.09 and 2361.55 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests recorded 25.47 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 13.03 GB/sec for large block writes. In higher-level execution, PassMark delivered an average CPU score of 6900.58 and a strong encryption result of 6460.91, while Redis reached 4.98 million SET operations per second.

From an infrastructure perspective, r5ad.2xlarge offers a cost-effective alternative to compute-heavy configurations when high RAM capacity and rapid scratch storage are prioritized over pure CPU clock speed. The presence of local NVMe eliminates standard network-attached storage latency for tempfiles and paging, though the lack of persistence requires replication architectures. Primary workloads include distributed caching nodes, medium-sized in-memory key-value databases, staging environments, and batch extract-transform-load (ETL) pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r5ad.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from a 4-core AMD EPYC 7571 processor at 2.2 GHz. Supported by the Nitro hypervisor, the instance includes 64.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation. Storage is augmented with a bundled 300 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume alongside a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps, with zero GPUs present. Benchmarks show modest single-thread CPU compute, highlighted by a Geekbench score of 727.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 6900.58, alongside balanced encryption and caching capabilities including 4.98 million Redis SET operations per second. The server provides strong memory density and local disk access for applications that require significant memory footprints without needing heavy per-core compute, making it well matched for in-memory key-value stores, ephemeral database caching, and intermediate data processing pipelines.
